title: Correctness of the uniform sampling algorithm
statement: For bit strings $w,r$ and a natural number $k$, encode the pair consisting of the encoding of $w$ with $k$ copies of the bit $1$ and the string $r$. The uniform-sampling algorithm on this input returns the empty string if none of the first $k$ consecutive blocks of length $\operatorname{size}(N-1)$ in $r$ has binary value less than $N$, where $N$ is the binary value of $w$; otherwise it returns a leading bit $1$ followed by the binary expansion of the first such block's value. In the displayed length, $\operatorname{size}$ is the binary length used by the algorithm.
caveat: The statement compares concrete encodings and an algorithm built from several auxiliary list-processing definitions; the prose summarizes their operational behavior.
